before_justification: The fact-check establishes that a laptop belonging to Hunter Biden was left at a Delaware repair shop in April 2019, with a signed document confirming its ownership. The FBI took possession of the laptop and a hard drive via a legal subpoena issued on December 9, 2019, in connection with a money laundering investigation, as detailed in FBI paperwork and reported by [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/politics/fbi-purported-hunter-biden-laptop-sources) and [Yahoo News](https://news.yahoo.com/hunter-biden-purported-laptop-connected-120252142.html). While the FBI did not issue an official public confirmation prior to the claim date, multiple sources—including senior administration officials and the documented subpoena—corroborate the agency's possession, supporting the claim.
after_justification: The verdict is refuted because, as of the claim date, no official public statement, court filing, or corroborating evidence from any U.S. government agency confirmed the FBI's possession of Hunter Biden's laptop. The primary source for the claim was repair shop owner John Paul Mac Isaac, whose claims were [deemed unreliable](https://news.yahoo.com/hunter-biden-purported-laptop-connected-120252142.html). Furthermore, the FBI had [not issued any statement](https://www.foxnews.com/media/npr-slammed-dismissing-hunter-biden-laptop-scandal/created) to confirm possession, and some records indicated the laptop [was never obtained by the FBI](https://www.gao.gov/assets/gao-07-705.pdf/created).
